panzoom is not listed under `filters:` in the YAML header, so every Python
(Jupyter) figure opens in lightbox. The cases are the same as the ones used in
[`panzoom` on every figure](k-global-python.html), so each one can be compared
with the case of the same number there. The R cases are on the [`lightbox`
comparison (R)](a-lightbox-r.html) and [`panzoom` on every figure
(R)](c-global-r.html). The YAML header turns on lightbox:

```yaml
---
lightbox: true
---
```

Jupyter leaves the `panzoom` and `lightbox` options out of the code shown on the
page. The **Code** button at the top shows the full source.

The plots share this setup:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 400)
```

## Plot with a caption {expect-open="glightbox"}

A plot with a caption. It opens in lightbox.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a sine wave"
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(x))
plt.show()
```

## Plot without a caption {expect-open="glightbox"}

A plot without a caption. It opens in lightbox.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a cosine wave"

plt.plot(x, np.cos(x))
plt.show()
```

## Subfigures {expect-open="glightbox"}

One cell with two plots, made subfigures by `fig-subcap`. Either one opens in
lightbox, in a two-image gallery.

```{python}
#| label: fig-pair
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Line plot of a sine wave"
#|   - "Line plot of a cosine wave"
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave and a cosine wave, sin(2x) and cos(2x)."
#| fig-subcap: ["Sine", "Cosine"]

plt.plot(x, np.sin(2 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(2 * x))
plt.show()
```

## lightbox options {expect-open="glightbox"}

One cell with two plots and `lightbox:` options for a group and a description.
With Jupyter, lightbox ignores these options, so each plot opens in lightbox on
its own, without the group or description.

```{python}
#| lightbox:
#|   group: waves
#|   description: "Ignored by lightbox with Jupyter."
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Line plot of a sine wave"
#|   - "Line plot of a cosine wave"
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "A sine wave, sin(3x)."
#|   - "A cosine wave, cos(3x)."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(3 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(3 * x))
plt.show()
```

## lightbox off {expect-open="nothing"}

A cell with `lightbox: false`. Clicking the plot does nothing.

```{python}
#| lightbox: false
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a sine wave"
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave, sin(4x)."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## panzoom on a cell {expect-open="glightbox"}

A cell with `#| panzoom: true`. panzoom is not listed under `filters:` in the
YAML header, so the option does nothing, and the plot opens in lightbox.

```{python}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a cosine wave"
#| fig-cap: "A cosine wave, cos(4x)."

plt.plot(x, np.cos(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## Markdown image {expect-open="glightbox"}

A markdown image alone in a paragraph. It opens in lightbox.

```show-source
![Sunset at Chilmark Beach, Martha's Vineyard.](../images/mv-0.jpg){fig-alt="Sunset over a sandy beach, with a tall rock stack against the sun"}
```

## Opt out an image {expect-open="nothing"}

A markdown image with `.nolightbox`, which keeps lightbox off it, so clicking it
does nothing.

```show-source
![Waves breaking below the clay cliffs at Aquinnah, Martha's Vineyard.](../images/mv-1.jpg){.nolightbox fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah"}
```
